newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close down after quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close down after quiet trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed down after a day of sluggish trading on markets in Bogota and Medellin.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell back 0.23 percent while Bogota's IBB index sunk 0.29 percent.
"The markets stayed quiet today and the paper that changed hands was in little-traded stocks which are not calculated within the index," one broker said in Bogota.
The Medellin index closed at 13,493.63 on a trading volume of 2.23 billion pesos and Bogota ended the session at 873.78 on a volume of 1.6 billion pesos.

The day's main mover in Medellin was a 1.8 billion pesos trade in cement company Cementos Rioclaro shares, part of the Sindicato Antioqueo conglomerate. The price of its shares slid back 10.3 percent to 2,609 pesos each.
"This was a cross deal in which one shareholder in the company needed liquidity and sold shares off to another shareholder at below market price," a Medellin broker explained.
Banco Ganadero's ordinary share price dropped back 1.4 percent to 282 pesos on the back of a trading volume of 15.8 million pesos.
"There was a price manipulation on these shares which had an impact despite the low volume traded," the dealer added.

Shares worth 130 million pesos in Compana Nacional de Chocolates changed hands at a stable 8,400 pesos per share. Suramericana de Seguros also remained stable at 18,500 pesos on a volume of 185 million pesos.
In Bogota, the day's major trade was in 600 million pesos of little-traded Banco Anglo Colombiano shares at a stable price of 60 pesos per share. The index was dented by drops in Banco Ganadero.
Ganadero's ordinary shares fell 1.04 percent to 283 and its preferential shares lost 1.57 percent, ending at 219 pesos a share.
"Shareholders moved to sell given Wednesaday's gains and to take profits after a long wait. The lack of liquidity in the market also affected decisions," one Bogota broker said.
